title: UK CertifID: making trust visible in registered digital verification services

content.text: OfDIA has authorised the first use of the UK CertifID trust mark by eligible digital verification service providers. UK CertifID will help people and businesses recognise services that meet government standards and appear on the digital verification services register (‘the register’).

Authorising the first use of UK CertifID is an important milestone for the UK market. It will give eligible services a clear and consistent way to show their registered status. Making registered services easier to recognise can help build customer confidence and support growth across the UK digital verification services market.
How UK CertifID makes registered services easier to recognise

Eligible services are now able to use UK CertifID for the first time. To be eligible, services must be certified against version 1.0 of the UK digital verification services trust framework, which came into force on 2 September 2026.
A consistent way for services to show their registered status

For providers of eligible services, UK CertifID turns their registered status into something customers can see more directly. Until now, there was no consistent way for services to visually show this to their customers. UK CertifID gives services an easier way to show their status in their apps, on their websites, marketing materials and in their bids for business.
Making trust visible for people and businesses

For people and businesses, UK CertifID helps to make trust visible. They can have greater confidence that wherever UK CertifID appears, the service has been certified as meeting government standards and is registered. As more eligible services are authorised to use UK CertifID, this should make it easier to distinguish services listed on the register from those that are not.
How to check a UK CertifID trust mark is genuine

Why a registered service may not display UK CertifID
We recommend eligible services use the UK CertifID trust mark but it is not mandatory to do so.

A service may be registered even if it does not display UK CertifID. For example, services certified against version gamma of the trust framework may appear on the register but are not eligible to use UK CertifID. If a service does not display UK CertifID, you can still search the register by service or provider name, to check they are listed.
If you are authorised to use UK CertifID and believe another organisation is using it without permission, tell us and your Conformity Assessment Body using your usual contact channels.

What happens next for UK CertifID

The UK CertifID trust mark is no longer just a concept. It’s real and it’s live. People and businesses should now begin to see UK CertifID on more eligible services. This is an important next step toward making trusted digital verification services easier to recognise.
If your service is eligible, you can now use UK CertifID to make your registered status visible, build customer confidence and support trust.
